VINIT.justification: The uninitialized state before any hadron exists; the void from which quark-antiquark pairs emerge.

TANCH.justification: The closed category of all known hadrons, bounded by the Σ-Ω plane and Frobenius constraint; no hadron lies outside this anchor.

AFWD.justification: Forward morphism that binds colored quarks into a colorless hadron, moving toward a stable singleton state.

AREV.justification: Contravariant morphism that breaks a hadron into lighter products, descending from stability to instability.

CLINK.justification: Sequential composition of gluon emissions and absorptions that chain together to form a hadronization event.

IMSCRIB.justification: Self-recognition of a hadron as a distinct species with fixed quantum numbers; it knows itself.

FSPLIT.justification: Branches a hadron state into its stoichiometry ratio (Σ) and topological winding (Ω) as two independent axes.

FFUSE.justification: Reconstitutes the hadron state from its Σ and Ω coordinates, recovering the original particle type exactly.

EVALT.justification: Affirmative evaluation: the hadron's (Σ,Ω) pair satisfies μ∘δ=id, granting topological protection against decay.

EVALF.justification: Negative evaluation: the (Σ,Ω) pair fails Frobenius closure, permitting decay via strong interaction.

ENGAGR.justification: Paradice state at the boundary between stability and instability, where the hadron both is a bound state and can dissociate without contradiction.

phase_3.both_description: A hadron at the critical boundary where μ∘δ=id holds marginally and decay channels are kinematically closed yet allowed — paradice of simultaneous stability and instability, e.g., certain tetraquark candidates.

steps.domain_action: QCD vacuum — void, no hadrons yet.
Standard Model boundary anchors the classification domain.
Quark confinement creates a hadron from a colored parton system.
Decompose the hadron into stoichiometry Σ and topological winding Ω axes.
Evaluate Σ-Ω pair against μ∘δ=id — if satisfied, mark as stable T-branch.
If μ∘δ=id fails, mark as unstable F-branch.
At the critical boundary, hold both stability and instability simultaneously.
Reconstruct the hadron from Σ-Ω via recomposition — recovers original input.
Chain multiple interactions (e.g., parton shower) to form complex hadrons.
The particle recognizes its own identity via conserved quantum numbers.
Simulate hadron decay back to lighter constituents (reverse morphism).
Permanent record of the classification in the PDG.
